module_title: Marketing and Selling Through Local Channels

lessons.title: Selling at Village Markets and Bus Parks
lessons.body: Selling at village markets and bus parks is one of the fastest ways to get cash for your chocolate and candy. Start by choosing the right days: most rural markets operate every 5 days, so find out the market calendar from local leaders. Arrive by 6 AM to secure a good spotânear the entrance or where buses park. A wooden table or a clean cloth on the ground works. Display your sweets in clear containers or wrappers so people see the colors. Price small candies at 50 shillings or 1 cedi each, and chocolate bars at 500 shillings or 2 cedis. Bus parks are busy in the morning (6-9 AM) and evening (4-7 PM) when travelers want snacks. Walk along the buses with a tray or basket, calling out, 'Sweet chocolate, fresh candy!' Keep change in a pouchâcoins and small notes. For every 10 candies you sell, you might make 500 shillings profit. Track what sells: if mint candies finish first, bring more next time. Be polite and smile; people buy from those they like. At the end of the day, count your money and note what you sold. Use a notebook to record sales. This helps you know how much to stock next market day. Also, watch for other sellersâif many sell candy, offer a unique flavor like ginger or coconut. You can also team up with a friend to cover more ground: one at the market, one at the bus park. Always keep your products clean and covered from dust. At bus parks, ask the conductor if you can board briefly to sell to passengersâsome allow it for a small fee. Remember, consistency matters. If you go every market day, people will know you and buy regularly. Start small with 100 candies and 20 chocolates; reinvest profits to grow.

lessons.title: Using WhatsApp and Facebook to Reach Customers
lessons.body: WhatsApp and Facebook are free tools to sell your chocolate and candy to more people. Start by creating a WhatsApp Business account (download the app, select 'Business'). Set your profile photo as a picture of your sweets, and write a status like 'Fresh homemade chocolates and candies. Order now!' Add your phone number and location. Post photos of your products dailyâuse natural light, show the sweets in your hand or on a clean plate. Write short captions: 'Mint candy â 50 KSh each. Buy 5 get 1 free.' Share your status updates to all contacts. Ask friends and family to forward your messages to their groups. On Facebook, create a page for your business (free). Post the same photos and captions. Join local buy-and-sell groups in your areaâsearch for 'Nairobi Buy and Sell' or 'Kampala Market'. Post your offer there, but follow group rules. Respond to comments quickly. Use WhatsApp to take orders: customers message you, you confirm price and delivery. For delivery, charge a small fee (e.g., 100 KSh within town) or meet at a central point. Offer mobile money payment (M-Pesa, Airtel Money, MTN MoMo). Keep a list of repeat customers in your phone contacts and send them a broadcast message when you have new stock. For example: 'New batch of dark chocolate ready! 500 KSh per bar. Reply to order.' You can also create a WhatsApp group for your best customers and give them exclusive discounts. To grow, ask satisfied customers to post a photo with your product and tag you. Run simple Facebook ads for as little as $1 per day targeting your town. But first, master free posting. Consistency is key: post at least 3 times a week. Track which posts get the most likes and commentsâmake more of those. Always reply within an hour during business hours. This builds trust and leads to more sales.

lessons.title: Partnering with Local Shops and Kiosks
lessons.body: Local shops and kiosks already have customers who buy snacks daily. Partnering with them means your chocolate and candy get seen by many people without you standing there. Start by identifying 5 shops near schools, bus stops, or markets. Visit the shop owner in the afternoon when they are less busy. Introduce yourself and show samples. Offer a simple deal: you supply the sweets at wholesale price, they sell at retail and keep the profit. For example, you sell a candy to them at 30 KSh, they sell at 50 KSh. For chocolate bars, you sell at 300 KSh, they sell at 500 KSh. Agree on a minimum order: start with 50 candies and 10 chocolates. Deliver fresh stock every week. Provide a small display box or jar with your label. Offer to take back unsold items if they are still in good conditionâthis reduces their risk. Some shop owners may ask for credit; start with small amounts and only after trust is built. Keep a record book: date, items given, amount due, amount paid. Collect payment weekly. To motivate them, offer a bonus: if they sell 100 candies in a month, give them 10 free. Also, ask them to recommend your sweets to customers. You can also partner with kiosks near schoolsâchildren buy candy after school. Provide colorful wrappers that attract kids. For kiosks, use small transparent jars so kids see the candy. Check in every few days to see what's selling and restock. If a shop sells well, give them a better margin or exclusive flavors. This encourages loyalty. Always be reliable: deliver on time and replace any damaged goods. Over time, you can have 10-20 shops selling for you, giving you steady income without market stress. Remember to calculate your costs: if you make a candy for 20 KSh and sell to shop at 30 KSh, you make 10 KSh profit per candy. With 20 shops each selling 50 candies a week, that's 1000 candies, 10,000 KSh profit weekly. That's real money.

lessons.title: Offering Free Samples to Build Trust
lessons.body: Free samples are a powerful way to convince people to buy your chocolate and candy. Many customers are afraid to spend money on something they haven't tasted. Give them a small piece and let the quality speak. Start by making tiny samples: cut a chocolate bar into 10 small squares, or offer one candy per person. Go to busy places: outside schools at closing time, at market entrances, or near bus parks. Stand with a tray and say, 'Free taste! Try my homemade chocolate.' Smile and offer it. Most people will take it. After they taste, ask, 'Would you like to buy some? A full bar is 500 KSh.' Many will buy on the spot. Keep a small stock with you. For every 20 samples you give, you might sell 5-10 items. That's a good return. Also, give samples to shop owners and kiosk ownersâthey need to taste before they agree to stock. When you give a sample, tell them your price and where they can buy. Hand out a small card with your WhatsApp number. At events like church gatherings or community meetings, ask permission to share samples. You can also include a free sample with every 10th purchase as a thank-you. This builds loyalty. Track your sampling: note how many samples you gave and how many sales resulted. If a particular flavor gets good reactions, make more of it. Be hygienic: use gloves or tongs, keep samples covered. Never give stale or broken piecesâit ruins trust. Over time, people will remember your brand and seek you out. Free samples cost you a little, but they bring repeat customers. For example, if you give 100 samples costing 500 KSh total, and you gain 20 new customers who each buy 2 bars a month, that's 20,000 KSh in monthly sales. Worth it.

lessons.title: Creating Loyalty Programs for Repeat Buyers
lessons.body: A loyalty program rewards customers who keep buying from you. It turns one-time buyers into regulars. Start simple: use a paper card or a small notebook. For every 10 candies a customer buys, give one free. Or for every 5 chocolate bars, give a free small candy. Tell customers about it when they buy. For example, 'Buy 5 bars and get a free mint candy.' Stamp or tick a card each time they buy. When the card is full, they redeem the reward. You can also use WhatsApp: keep a list of loyal customers and send them a special code for 10% off their next order. Another idea: a points system. Each 100 KSh spent earns 1 point. 10 points = 100 KSh off. Keep a record in a notebook or use a free app like Loyverse. For illiterate customers, use a simple card with symbols. Make the program easy to understand. Promote it on your WhatsApp status and Facebook page. Announce: 'Join our loyalty club! Buy 10 get 1 free.' Offer a birthday reward: free chocolate on their birthday if they show ID. This makes customers feel special. Also, give a referral bonus: if a customer brings a new buyer, both get a free candy. Track your loyal customersâthey are your best marketers. Send them a message when you have new flavors. For example, 'New dark chocolate with almonds! Loyal customers get 20% off this week.' This encourages repeat purchases. Keep the program simple and consistent. Don't change rules often. If you use a card, ask customers to keep it safe. You can also partner with a shop: when customers buy from that shop, they get a stamp from you. Over time, you'll see more repeat sales. For example, if 50 customers buy weekly because of the loyalty program, your income becomes predictable. You can plan production better. Start with a small group of 20 loyal customers and grow from there.

lessons.title: Participating in Trade Fairs and Festivals
lessons.body: Trade fairs and festivals bring many people together in a festive moodâperfect for selling chocolate and candy. Look for events in your area: agricultural shows, cultural festivals, school fun days, church bazaars, or national holidays. Register early. Booth fees vary: from 5,000 to 50,000 KSh depending on the event. Choose a booth in a high-traffic area, near the entrance or food section. Decorate your stall: use bright cloth, balloons, and a banner with your business name and WhatsApp number. Display your sweets attractively: use tiered trays, clear jars, and sample plates. Offer free samples to passersby. Price for the event: you can charge slightly more because people are in a spending mood, but don't overdo it. For example, sell a chocolate bar at 600 KSh instead of 500 KSh. Offer festival specials: 'Festival pack: 5 candies for 200 KSh.' Bring enough stock: estimate 200-500 items per day. Also bring change, a cash box, and a notebook to record sales. At festivals, people want quick service. Have pre-packed bags ready. Use a helper to handle money while you serve. Engage customers: ask them to try a sample, tell them about your ingredients. Collect phone numbers for your WhatsApp listâoffer a small discount for those who join. You can also collaborate with other vendors: a juice seller might let you put a small display on their table for a share of profits. After the event, follow up with new contacts on WhatsApp: 'Thank you for trying our chocolate at the fair! Here's a 10% discount for your first order.' Track which events gave the best sales. Repeat the good ones. For example, a three-day trade fair might cost 20,000 KSh but bring 100,000 KSh in sales. That's a great return. Always have business cards or flyers with your contact. Festivals are also great for learning what new flavors people like. Ask for feedback. Use the opportunity to build your brand and network with other entrepreneurs.

quiz.q: What is the best time to arrive at a village market to get a good selling spot?
quiz.explanation: Arriving early, around 6 AM, secures a prime location before other sellers arrive.

quiz.q: At a bus park, when are the busiest times for selling snacks?
quiz.explanation: Travelers are most active during morning and evening rush hours, making those the best selling times.

quiz.q: What should you use to display candies at a market to attract buyers?
quiz.explanation: Clear containers or wrappers allow customers to see the colorful candies, which attracts attention.

quiz.q: Why is it important to keep a notebook when selling at markets?
options: B) To record sales and track what sells best
quiz.explanation: Recording sales helps you know how much to stock next time and which products are most popular.

quiz.q: What is a good price for a small candy at a village market according to the lesson?
quiz.explanation: The lesson suggests pricing small candies at 50 shillings or 1 cedi each.

quiz.q: How can you use WhatsApp Business to sell your products?
options: A) Only send messages to family
B) Post photos and status updates, take orders
C) Use it to play games
quiz.explanation: WhatsApp Business allows you to showcase products, update status, and receive orders directly.

quiz.q: What type of photo is best for your WhatsApp profile?
options: B) A picture of your sweets
quiz.explanation: A clear picture of your sweets helps customers instantly recognize what you sell.

quiz.q: On Facebook, where can you post your products to reach local buyers?
options: C) On your personal page only
quiz.explanation: Local buy-and-sell groups are filled with people in your area looking to buy goods.

quiz.q: What is a good way to accept payment when selling via WhatsApp?
quiz.explanation: Mobile money is widely used and convenient for both seller and buyer in many African countries.

quiz.q: How often should you post on social media to keep customers engaged?
options: B) At least 3 times a week
C) Only when you have new stock
quiz.explanation: Consistent posting keeps your business visible and reminds customers to buy.

quiz.q: What is a key benefit of partnering with local shops?
options: A) You don't have to make products
B) Your products reach more customers without you being there
C) You can sell at higher prices
quiz.explanation: Shops already have foot traffic, so your products get seen by many potential buyers.

quiz.q: What is a typical wholesale price for a candy if you sell to a shop at 30 KSh?
quiz.explanation: The lesson states you sell a candy to the shop at 30 KSh, and they sell at 50 KSh.

quiz.q: Why might you offer to take back unsold items from a shop?
options: A) To reduce the shop owner's risk
quiz.explanation: Taking back unsold goods lowers the shop owner's risk, making them more willing to partner with you.

quiz.q: How often should you collect payment from a shop you supply?
quiz.explanation: Weekly payment collection is manageable and keeps records clear.

quiz.q: What is a good way to motivate a shop to sell more of your products?
options: B) Offer a bonus for high sales
quiz.explanation: A bonus, like free items after selling a certain amount, encourages the shop to push your products.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of offering free samples?
options: A) To give away all your stock
B) To build trust and convince people to buy
quiz.explanation: Free samples let customers taste the quality, reducing their fear of buying something unknown.

quiz.q: Where is a good place to give out free samples?
options: A) Outside schools at closing time
C) At night in empty streets
quiz.explanation: Schools at closing time have many potential customers, especially children who like sweets.

quiz.q: How many samples might you give to make 5-10 sales?
quiz.explanation: The lesson suggests for every 20 samples, you might sell 5-10 items.

quiz.q: What should you do after someone tastes a free sample?
options: B) Ask if they want to buy
D) Give them more free samples
quiz.explanation: Asking for the sale right after they taste increases the chance of a purchase.

quiz.q: What is a simple loyalty program idea mentioned in the lesson?
quiz.explanation: A common loyalty program is giving a free item after a certain number of purchases, like buy 10 get 1 free.

quiz.q: How can you track loyalty points for customers who cannot read?
options: B) Use a card with symbols
quiz.explanation: Using symbols or pictures on a card makes it easy for non-literate customers to understand their progress.

quiz.q: What is a referral bonus?
options: A) A discount for bringing a new customer
B) A free product for the seller
C) A penalty for not buying
quiz.explanation: A referral bonus rewards existing customers for bringing in new buyers, often giving both a reward.

quiz.q: Why is it important to keep loyalty program rules consistent?
options: B) To build trust and avoid disappointment
quiz.explanation: Consistent rules help customers know what to expect, which builds trust and encourages participation.

quiz.q: How can a loyalty program help your business?
options: B) It turns one-time buyers into regulars
quiz.explanation: Loyalty programs incentivize repeat purchases, creating a steady customer base.

quiz.q: What should you do before participating in a trade fair?
options: A) Register early and pay the booth fee
quiz.explanation: Registering early secures a good spot and ensures you are included in the event.

quiz.q: How can you decorate your stall at a festival to attract customers?
options: A) Use bright cloth, balloons, and a banner
quiz.explanation: Bright decorations and clear signage make your stall noticeable and inviting.

quiz.q: Why might you charge slightly more at a festival?
options: A) People are in a spending mood
quiz.explanation: Festival-goers are often willing to spend more on treats, so a small price increase is acceptable.

quiz.q: What should you bring to a trade fair to handle many customers?
quiz.explanation: Having sufficient stock and change ensures you can serve customers quickly without running out.

quiz.q: How can you follow up with new contacts after a fair?
options: A) Send a WhatsApp message with a discount
quiz.explanation: A friendly WhatsApp message with a special offer reminds them of your product and encourages a first order.

quiz.q: What is a good way to measure if a trade fair was successful?
options: A) Count how many people attended
B) Track sales and new contacts
C) See how many flyers you gave
D) Count the hours you stood
quiz.explanation: Sales and new customer contacts are direct indicators of the fair's return on investment.
